To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the active‐layer thickness of a (Al,GaAs double‐hetrostructure laser is often nonuniform due to the presence of growth defects; (2) the growth defects are quantified by angle‐lap measurements; (3) the optical scattering losses are computed as functions of the growth defect parameters; and (4) the threshold currents are computed for lasers having the measured growth defect parameters.

the threshold current variations of (Al,Gal)As DH lasers can be attributed to the presence of optical scatterers in the active‐layer gain region and the scatterers can be characterized by angle‐lap measurements of the epitaxial surface morphology.

(1) the active‐layer thickness variations of (Al,Gal)As double‐ heterostructure lasers can be characterized by angle‐lap measurements, and (2) the optical‐ scattering losses introduced by these variations can be calculated from the angle‐lap data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the active‐layer thickness variations and optical scattering on the threshold current of the (Al,Ga,As) double‐heterojunction laser.
the effects of growth defects on the threshold current of (Al,GaN) double‐heterojunction lasers.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the V–I threshold current variations in (Al,Gal)As double‐ heterostructure lasers are due to the existence of optical scattering disturbances in the gain volume.
the optical‐scattering loss in the active layer is the major cause for the V _{3} threshold current variations in (Al,Gal)As double‐Heterostructure lasers.
the optical losses in (AlGa)As double‐ heterostructure lasers are dominated by the optical scattering losses which are introduced by the active‐layer growth defects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
optical scattering losses due to growth defects are significant and must be considered when evaluating the threshold current of (Al,GaNAs) DH lasers.
the V _{th} of the laser diode depends on the scattering losses of the waveguide and that the scattering losses depend on the surface morphology of the waveguide.
the threshold current of the (Al,Ga,As) double‐heterojunction laser is sensitive to the presence of growth defects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optical scattering losses are strongly dependent on the local waveguide deformation.
the optical losses due to the defects in the active‐layer gain region can be quite significant, even for the relatively low‐power threshold operation of the (Al,Ga,As double‐hetastructure laser.
optical scattering can be an important loss mechanism in double‐heterojunction lasers.
